checklist.answer: To configure your OAuth consent screen, go to the Google API Console and navigate to Menu menu > Google Auth platform > Branding.
Under App Information, you must enter an App name and choose a User support email. Under Contact Information, you must enter an Email address.

Visit the Google API Console to obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials such as a client ID and client secret that are known to both Google and your application. For example, a JavaScript application does not require a secret, but a web server application does.
Authorization scopes are OAuth 2.0 URI strings that contain the Google Workspace app name, data accessed, and level of access. They are categorized as non-sensitive, sensitive, and restricted.

To publish an app publicly to the Google Workspace Marketplace, Google reviews your app and its listing to make sure they meet Google's design, content, and style guidelines. After Google reviews your app, you receive an email about whether it needs more work or if it's approved.
“Most verification requests receive a response within 24 to 72 hours.”
Unverified Apps Script projects using sensitive scopes and accessed by users outside the domain will display an unverified app screen and have a cap on the number of unverified users.

Common reasons an app doesn't pass review include incorrect OAuth consent screen set up (such as user type set to Internal or publishing status set to Testing), the app didn't complete the OAuth verification, inappropriate use of Google's trademarks in the app name, logo, or app descriptions, and issues where links don't work or screenshots are of low quality. Other reasons include the app still being tested and not publicly ready, or having bugs and not being fully functional.
